about: The `eventexpr` of a <send> is a string computed from the machine's fields when the send runs, and names the event the send delivers: `name` holds `ping` to begin with, so `go` delivers `ping`; `use.pong` makes it `pong`, and the same <send> then delivers `pong`. A name that is empty names no event: an argument that cannot be evaluated, so error.execution is raised and nothing is sent. The machine goes on once the name is a name again. A name that cannot be computed is the same argument error: `overflow` sends one whose product does not fit its type, and nothing is delivered. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: the name the machine holds is the event delivered
and again: the send reads the name each time it runs
the name changes; nothing is sent
the same send delivers the other event now
an empty name names no event
the send is an argument that cannot be evaluated: reported, and nothing delivered
the name is a name again, and the machine goes on
a name whose computation overflows is an argument that cannot be evaluated: reported, nothing delivered
